design:
## Design tests

After the bench, the new drawings were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v025.md`, six pictures, three readers). The bag was "a yellow shopping bag" in all three of its pictures with no hedge, on the older man too. The bird was at the food in all three, "about to eat or take her lunch", with no remark on its size. The roller was "a long-handled paint roller" or "a roller or brush" against the fence, and no reader remarked on the barrow's shadow. The tan newspaper dog read in full with its own paws on the paper. The white dog, small on pale paving in the busiest picture, was "an odd white figure, like a white dog or a person": one reader, so no rule, left for the screen to count. No new rule came out of them, so there was no second round.
intro: The twenty-second screen read all 68 pictures, the set's 21 and 47 probes: 779 of 785 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. The bag, the gate's one failure in v0.24, rose from 0.75 to 1.00, "a yellow shopping bag". No reader said kettle, gloves or a shadow too large. But 61 of the 64 templates pass the gate, down from 63: three that this release did not change fall short, each on one or two half marks and each in full in v0.24. The v0.9 retest put the gate's reader variance at about five templates between screens, so this does not by itself show that anything got worse, and `vision/flaws_v025.md` lists what to look at for v0.26 all the same. Above all, the older man's face, the most repeated specific remark.
screen:
Across all 68 pictures 779 of 785 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. Below full marks: a dog by the door "with its eyes shut", its wish for a walk never stated; the clouds, not mentioned in one description; a duck "swimming towards the food", twice, its purpose only implied; an older man "as if sweeping" who "could be ... pausing to watch"; and a floating box called cardboard.

**Oddities now come in two rows.** Scorers differ in how much they log (83% of the readers' remarks in v0.24, 22% in v0.23), so `summarize_screen.py` now counts the remarks in the readers' "unsure" sections directly, for every screen, and the scorer prompt caps its list at three per picture. Remarks rose again, to 6.29 per picture (5.67), so this release did not bring the total down: what it removed were named complaints. Current readers write about 15% more than the v0.23 readers on the same pictures (the v0.24 control), and how much of the rest is readers, pictures or their mix is not separated. What they noticed: the older man's face, in ten of his 21 pictures ("hard to read", "an odd grey patch"); the newspaper dog's head ("a monkey, an otter", "a spacesuit or a small robot"); a backwards cap as a head "the wrong way round"; and figures overlapping the pond.
redrawn: The bag read in full in all three of its pictures, and the bird, the roller and the newspaper dog in all of theirs. The three that fail the gate are in the table too, as none of them was changed: each read in full in v0.24.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (51 in three, 7 in four, 1 in five, 3 in six, 2 in seven), and 61 of 64 pass, down from 63. All three failures are on templates this release did not change, and read in full in v0.24. The v0.9 retest put the gate's reader variance at about five templates between screens, so the gate is a filter and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
inspection: Building and inspecting the set and the probes found nothing more to fix. The tier-4 garden and park placed again on their v0.24 seeds with the same events. The tier-4 street took three searches side by side and 13 failed seeds, the tier-4 playground two searches and 3 failed seeds, and the tier-3 playground again the unsteered search after 13 failed seeds under template-variety steering. The tier-4 isomorph came within 13 tries (about 230 in v0.24). The set's isomorphs are two at tier 2, two at tier 3 and one at tier 4. All 68 records rebuild identical to the pixel.
calib: The bird at the sandwich's cue salience moved by -0.32 with its smaller size, and the newspaper dog's by +0.08 with the paper behind it; every other template's by at most 0.001.
